items.label: DESIGN SYSTEM
items.title:
Structure
first,
always
items.desc: Start with tokens and code structure before anything else — clear folder layout, well-separated concerns. So future-me comes back in 3 months and still understands everything.
bullets: No magic numbers in the codebase

items.label: FRONTEND DEV
items.title:
Good UI
doesn't need
explaining
items.desc: Every interaction should feel smooth and intuitive — from button press to error message. Great UX means the user never notices anything is wrong.
bullets: Animations with intent, not just effect

items.label: BACKEND & API
items.title:
Design from
use case,
not framework
items.desc: Design the API from use cases first — clear structure, complete error handling. Makes frontend work easy and debugging fast, even as a solo developer.
bullets: Error messages the frontend can reuse
API docs that stay up to date

items.label: DEPLOYMENT
items.title:
Deploy and
never babysit
the server
items.desc: Deployment shouldn't be nerve-wracking — keep Dev and Production clearly separated, manage env properly, then push with confidence.
bullets: Know when it breaks before users do

items.label: CODE QUALITY
items.title:
Code that's
still readable
months later
items.desc: Good code is both readable and fast — if a function has a heavy query or is hard to follow, fix it immediately rather than letting it accumulate.
bullets: Catch heavy queries before users do
Leave comments, because you'll forget too
